title.narrative: iOc2.1 Number of processors and traders supported by the project

description.narrative: Processors in this context are defined as any enterprise(s) use of at least one motorised cassava processing equipment; employs at least 35 workers; processes approximately more than two (2) metric tonnes of cassava daily; operates in a defined territory that processes raw cassava from its natural state into value added products/cassava derivatives. Traders in this context are enterprises who buy and sell cassava and cassava derivatives/products. Supported enterprises will be enterprises which will directly benefit from project activities including training, financial and/or equipment support & linkage(s) to other cassava value chain actors in an IPPCs

comment.narrative: The project is looking at supporting 5 enterprises within the selected five counties.
At the end of project year 1 5 enterprises 3 in Grand Gedeh 1 Maryland 1 River Gee have been supported by the project.

description.narrative: Entrepreneurs in this context are people who have established or aim to establish any enterprise within the cassava value chain (off takers/processors). Actor (economic entity) operating along the value chain including all upstream (producer, input supplier)/downstream (processor, marketer), support functions (transport, financing etc.). An entrepreneur generates an individual income, create employment and acquire resources from third parties and creates value along the chain (value creation value capture and value distribution).

comment.narrative: As at the first implementing year 5 entrepreneurs have been trained by the project 3 men 2 women 1 youth

description.narrative: Entrepreneurs in this context are people who have established or aim to establish any enterprise within the cassava value chain (off takers/processors). Actor (economic entity) operating along the value chain including all upstream (producer, input supplier)/downstream (processor, marketer), support functions (transport, financing etc.). An entrepreneur generates an individual income, create employment and acquire resources from third parties and creates value along the chain (value creation value capture and value distribution).

comment.narrative: The availability and access to improved and healthy planting material for cassava production is a major challenge in the project area. According to the project baseline 95 of farmers resort to the use of traditional planting materials sourced from their own farms. The continuous use of the same planting resource has resulted in decreased viability as they become prone to pests and diseases. Cassava mosaic virus which can lead to up to 8090 yield loss is common in the production area.The establishment of nurseries for cassava planting material is necessary to assure the availability of diseasefree cassava cuttings. Farmers expressed willingness to pay for improved cuttings if only they are available and easily accessible to them. The project thence floated a proposal to support the establishment of a privatelyoperated nurseries in the project landscape. Agro Green Inc Citizen Farms Inc. and Natemujee Agro Resources expressed interest to establish and operate nurseries.

description.narrative: The UN Convention on the rights of Persons with Disability (http://www.un.org/esa/socdev/enable/rights/convtexte.htm 6 December 2006)Preamble (e) defines PwDs: Recognizing that disability is an evolving concept and that disability results from the interaction between persons with impairments and attitudinal and environmental barriers that hinders their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. For the purposes of this project the most important articles of the convention shall be:Art 17: Protecting the integrity of the person Art 19(b)(c): Living independently and being included in community Art 21: Freedom of expression and opinion and access to information Art 24(5): education vocational training and lifelong learning without discrimination Art 27(c)(d)(e)(f)(k): work and employment (c) labour rights; (d) effective access to general vocational and technical guidance programme (e) promotion of employment opportunities and career advancement (f) promotion of opportunities for selfemployment, entrepreneurship, development of cooperatives and starting ones own business. (k) promotion of vocational and professional rehabilitation.
